objectives: Read the geologic time scale from Hadean to Anthropocene.
Apply radiometric dating + biostratigraphy + magnetostratigraphy to deep-time problems.
Interpret GSSP Golden Spikes + the formal chronostratigraphic apparatus.

slides.title: Eons + eras + periods + epochs: the architecture of deep time
slides.body:
The **geologic time scale (GTS)** is the formal hierarchical division of Earth's 4.54-Gyr history. Compiled + revised by the **International Commission on Stratigraphy (ICS)** — the current authoritative version is **Cohen et al. 2013, updated v2023** (Kim Cohen + colleagues), available as an open chart at stratigraphy.org. The scale has four hierarchical levels:

**Eons** (longest): Hadean → Archean → Proterozoic → Phanerozoic. The first three together are sometimes called the **Precambrian** + cover ~88% of Earth history but produce only sparse fossil record.
- **Hadean** (4.54-4.0 Gya) — formation, Moon-forming impact (Theia), magma ocean, Jack Hills zircons (Wilde et al. 2001) are the oldest preserved minerals at 4.4 Gya.
- **Archean** (4.0-2.5 Gya) — first cells (~3.5+ Gya), microbial mats + stromatolites, banded iron formations, anoxic atmosphere.
- **Proterozoic** (2.5 Gya - 538.8 Mya) — Great Oxidation Event ~2.4 Gya, eukaryogenesis ~2 Gya, Snowball Earth episodes (Sturtian + Marinoan, ~720 + 635 Mya), Ediacaran biota (~575-541 Mya).
- **Phanerozoic** ('visible life', 538.8 Mya - present) — the period covered by most paleontology.

**Eras** (within Phanerozoic):
- **Paleozoic** (538.8-251.9 Mya): Cambrian → Ordovician → Silurian → Devonian → Carboniferous → Permian. Marine invertebrate radiations, first land plants + tetrapods, ends in Permian-Triassic mass extinction.
- **Mesozoic** (251.9-66 Mya): Triassic → Jurassic → Cretaceous. 'Age of Reptiles' + dinosaurs + first mammals + birds + flowering plants; ends in K-Pg mass extinction.
- **Cenozoic** (66 Mya - present): Paleogene (Paleocene + Eocene + Oligocene) → Neogene (Miocene + Pliocene) → Quaternary (Pleistocene + Holocene). 'Age of Mammals' + grasslands + Quaternary glaciations + the human lineage.

**Periods + epochs**: the next two finer levels. Every named subdivision corresponds to a global stratigraphic unit (the **chronostratigraphic units**: Eonothem → Erathem → System → Series → Stage) — every '*period*' (time interval) has a paired '*system*' (rock record).

**The Anthropocene proposal**: in 2009 + after the Anthropocene Working Group (AWG, **Jan Zalasiewicz** Chair) was convened. The AWG recommended (2019) formally adopting the Anthropocene as an epoch with base at ~1952 (plutonium fallout from atmospheric nuclear tests + correlated stratigraphic markers). In **March 2024** the ICS Subcommission on Quaternary Stratigraphy voted **against** ratifying it — the Anthropocene remains an informal but widely used term, not yet a chronostratigraphic unit. (Many geoscientists continue to advocate for its formal recognition; the debate is ongoing.)

The GTS embeds a remarkable consensus: ~150 international scientists from ICS subcommissions vote on every boundary + name. By convention rocks below a boundary are 'older'; rocks above are 'younger'. The whole apparatus rests on three orthogonal dating methods covered next.

slides.title: Radiometric, bio-, and magnetostratigraphic dating
slides.body:
Three orthogonal dating methods establish the geologic time scale:

**Radiometric dating** — measures the decay of radioactive isotopes (parent) to stable daughters in mineral crystals; the ratio gives absolute age via the radioactive decay law $N(t) = N_0 e^{-\lambda t}$.
- **U-Pb on zircon** — the gold standard for deep time. Zircon (ZrSiO₄) incorporates uranium but excludes lead during crystallization → all Pb is radiogenic. Two parallel decay chains: ²³⁸U → ²⁰⁶Pb ($t_{1/2}$ = 4.468 Gyr) + ²³⁵U → ²⁰⁷Pb ($t_{1/2}$ = 704 Myr). Concordia diagrams give discordia ages even when crystals are slightly disturbed. **Clair Patterson** (1956) used U-Pb on meteorites to date the Earth at **4.55 ± 0.07 Gyr** — the modern value. Modern ID-TIMS + LA-ICP-MS U-Pb routinely date Phanerozoic ash beds to ±0.1% precision.
- **K-Ar + Ar-Ar** — ⁴⁰K → ⁴⁰Ar ($t_{1/2}$ = 1.25 Gyr). Useful from ~50 kya to billions of years. Ar-Ar (Merrihue + Turner 1966) is the modern variant, more precise. Critical for dating volcanic ashes that bracket fossil-bearing strata.
- **¹⁴C carbon-14** — ¹⁴N + n → ¹⁴C; ¹⁴C → ¹⁴N ($t_{1/2}$ = 5730 yr). Range: ~50 kya - present. **Willard Libby** (1908-1980) developed the method in 1949 (Chemistry Nobel 1960). Calibration via tree rings + speleothems + corals (IntCal2020). Indispensable for Quaternary paleontology, archaeology, climate science.
- **Cosmogenic nuclides** — ¹⁰Be, ²⁶Al, ³⁶Cl produced by cosmic-ray bombardment of surface rocks; concentrations measure exposure time (10s yr - Myr). Used for dating Quaternary glaciations, hominin sites, denudation rates.
- **U-series** — ²³⁰Th / ²³⁴U disequilibrium in speleothems + corals + bones — 10s kya - 500 kya range.
- **OSL + TL** — optically + thermally stimulated luminescence dates the last sun- or heat-exposure of quartz grains. ka - 200 ka range.

**Biostratigraphy** — uses **index fossils** to correlate strata globally. The principle (William Smith 1815 — faunal succession) is augmented by the modern recognition that **first appearance datums (FADs)** + **last appearance datums (LADs)** of taxa form correlative horizons. Different groups dominate different intervals:
- **Trilobites + brachiopods** — Cambrian to Permian.
- **Conodonts** — Cambrian to Triassic; one of the most precise biostratigraphic tools.
- **Graptolites** — Ordovician to Devonian.
- **Ammonites** — Devonian to Cretaceous; pristine Mesozoic biostratigraphy.
- **Foraminifera + nannofossils** — Mesozoic to recent; the basis of marine micropaleontology + petroleum exploration.
- **Mammal teeth** — Cenozoic continental sequences (NALMA + ELMA + ALMA stages).

**Magnetostratigraphy** — Earth's magnetic field reverses polarity irregularly; the **Geomagnetic Polarity Time Scale (GPTS)** is calibrated by radiometric dating of marine + continental sequences with magnetic-mineral records. The **Cande + Kent 1995** GPTS is the standard. The Brunhes-Matuyama reversal (currently dated 773 ka, Singer 2019) is a classic Quaternary marker. Magnetostratigraphy is especially powerful where fossils are sparse + volcanic ashes are absent.

**Walther's Law of facies (1894)** — facies that are deposited side-by-side in a single environment (e.g., beach + lagoon + offshore) are stacked vertically as the shoreline migrates. Modern **sequence stratigraphy** (Vail + Mitchum + Posamentier, 1970s-80s, Exxon) extends Walther's logic to interpret transgression-regression cycles + global sea level. Sequence stratigraphy is the dominant interpretive framework in petroleum geology + modern stratigraphic correlation.

When radiometric + bio- + magnetostratigraphy + sequence stratigraphy converge on the same chronology — which they generally do — the geologic time scale stands on a foundation as solid as any in science.

slides.title: Chronostratigraphy + GSSP Golden Spikes
slides.body:
**Chronostratigraphy** is the formal classification of rock strata by their age — distinct from **lithostratigraphy** (by rock type), **biostratigraphy** (by fossil content), or **magnetostratigraphy** (by magnetic polarity). The chronostratigraphic hierarchy is:

**Eonothem ⊃ Erathem ⊃ System ⊃ Series ⊃ Stage**

(time equivalents: Eon, Era, Period, Epoch, Age)

Every chronostratigraphic unit — every boundary in deep time — is defined by a **Global Boundary Stratotype Section + Point (GSSP)**, colloquially called a **'Golden Spike'**. A GSSP is a specific outcrop chosen by international vote to physically embody the boundary. Golden Spikes are literally bronze markers driven into the rock; they are world heritage sites of stratigraphy.

**Why GSSPs?** Before the 1970s, boundaries were defined by their type localities (often regionally restricted). The **Hedberg 1976 International Stratigraphic Guide** + the **Salvador 1994** revision adopted the GSSP system: a single point in a single section globally defines the boundary; the same boundary is then *correlated* worldwide using available tools (fossils, isotopes, paleomagnetism). This shifts the question from 'where is the Cambrian-Ordovician boundary in *my* outcrop?' to 'how do *my* outcrop's signals correlate to the GSSP?'

**Examples of GSSPs**:
- **Cambrian-Ordovician GSSP** — Green Point, Newfoundland, Canada (2000). Defined by FAD of conodont *Iapetognathus fluctivagus*.
- **Permian-Triassic GSSP** — Meishan, Zhejiang, China (2001). Defined by FAD of conodont *Hindeodus parvus*; the layer corresponds to the largest mass extinction in Earth history (252.0 Mya).
- **K-Pg GSSP** — El Kef, Tunisia (1991). Defined by Ir anomaly + extinction horizon (66.0 Mya).
- **Holocene GSSP** — NorthGRIP ice core, Greenland (2009). Defined in an ice core, not a rock outcrop — the first ice-based GSSP.

The formal definitions matter because once a GSSP is voted in, all global stratigraphers use the same reference. Boundaries are conceptually fixed in time even if they cannot be physically observed in any local section.

**The construction of the modern GTS** (Cohen, Finney, Gibbard, Fan + colleagues — Episodes 2013 + updated): each boundary is now defined either by an existing GSSP or by a global standard stratigraphic age (GSSA) for older + Precambrian boundaries. **Numerical ages** for boundaries are derived from astronomical tuning of Milankovitch cycles (orbital eccentricity 100/400-kyr, obliquity 41-kyr, precession 21-kyr) — which has revolutionized late-Cenozoic chronology — + from U-Pb on interbedded ash beds (the **Bouligand et al. 2019** dating revision of the Cenozoic, the **Schoene et al. 2019** dating of K-Pg Deccan + Chicxulub).

**Why the timeline viz matters**: the embedded **extinction-timeline** visualization shows the geologic time scale with the Big Five mass extinctions (Ordovician-Silurian 445 Mya, Late Devonian 372 Mya, Permian-Triassic 252 Mya, Triassic-Jurassic 201 Mya, K-Pg 66 Mya) overlaid on Sepkoski's diversity curve. Notice (1) the long flat Cambrian-Ordovician rise; (2) the Permian-Triassic catastrophe (~96% marine species lost); (3) the Cenozoic + modern radiations. **Recovery curves** after each extinction take 5-30 Myr — the empirical signature of macroevolutionary resilience.

The GTS is the spinal column of the rest of the path: every fossil's age, every extinction's date, every evolutionary radiation's tempo + mode is defined relative to this framework. Next: **taphonomy** — how organisms become fossils.

question.question: Compute a radiometric age from U-Pb ratios
question.goal: Given a zircon with measured ²⁰⁶Pb / ²³⁸U = 0.0858, derive the age using the decay law.

steps.prompt: The decay equation is $N(t) = N_0 e^{-\lambda t}$. For U-Pb, the daughter abundance is D = N₀ - N. Express the ratio D/N in terms of λ + t.
hints: D = N₀ - N + N = N₀ e^(-λt).
steps.reveal: $D = N_0 - N$; divide by $N$: $D/N = (N_0/N) - 1 = e^{\lambda t} - 1$. So $t = (1/\lambda) \ln(1 + D/N)$.

steps.prompt: ²³⁸U has $\lambda_{238} = 1.5513 \times 10^{-10}$ yr⁻¹ (corresponding to $t_{1/2}$ = 4.468 Gyr). Compute t for D/N = 0.0858.
steps.reveal:
$t = \ln(1.0858) / (1.5513 \times 10^{-10}) = 0.0823 / (1.5513 \times 10^{-10}) \approx 5.30 \times 10^{8}$ yr ≈ **530 Myr**. Note this is approximately the Cambrian-Ediacaran boundary (538.8 Myr).

In practice, the analyst would also measure ²⁰⁷Pb / ²³⁵U + plot on concordia (Wetherill 1956) to check for Pb loss; with both ratios concordant, the age is robust.

steps.prompt: Why is zircon the preferred mineral for U-Pb deep-time dating?

acceptedAnswers: Zircon incorporates U but excludes Pb; chemically robust + retains Pb; resists metamorphism

steps.reveal: Zircon (ZrSiO₄): (1) incorporates U⁴⁺ (similar ionic radius to Zr⁴⁺) but excludes Pb²⁺ during crystallization → all measured Pb is radiogenic; (2) chemically + mechanically robust — survives sedimentary recycling + metamorphism; (3) high closure temperature (>900 °C) — Pb does not diffuse out unless the crystal melts. These properties make zircon the workhorse for dating felsic igneous rocks + their derived sediments. Jack Hills zircons (4.4 Gya) are the oldest known minerals on Earth — preserved in younger sandstones.

steps.prompt: What other dating methods would you use to corroborate this U-Pb age?

acceptedAnswers: Ar-Ar on biotite or sanidine; biostratigraphy via index fossils; magnetostratigraphy

steps.reveal: Multi-proxy validation: (1) **Ar-Ar** on biotite or sanidine grains from the same ash bed — independent decay system, comparable precision; (2) **biostratigraphy** — match the fossil assemblage to the Cambrian-Ediacaran boundary fauna; (3) **magnetostratigraphy** — match observed reversal pattern; (4) **chemostratigraphy** — δ¹³C excursions (BACE — Basal Cambrian Carbon Excursion). When all four converge on ~538 Myr, you have a robust chronostratigraphic correlation.

question.question: What is a **GSSP (Global Boundary Stratotype Section + Point, 'Golden Spike')** + why does the formal apparatus matter?
options: A **GSSP** is a single stratigraphic section + point — physically marked with a bronze plaque — chosen by international vote (under the ICS) to formally define a chronostratigraphic boundary. Examples: Cambrian-Ordovician at Green Point Newfoundland (2000); Permian-Triassic at Meishan China (2001); K-Pg at El Kef Tunisia (1991); Holocene base in the NorthGRIP ice core (2009). The point is selected because it (1) lies in a continuous, well-preserved, accessible section; (2) hosts identifiable global markers — typically the first appearance of an index fossil (e.g., conodont *Hindeodus parvus* for the PT boundary) + chemical anomalies (Ir at K-Pg) + magnetic signatures. **Why it matters**: before GSSPs, boundary definitions varied by tradition, making global correlation contentious. GSSPs fix boundaries in a single physical reference; all other sections are correlated *to* the GSSP via biostratigraphy + isotope chemistry + magnetostratigraphy + sequence stratigraphy. The Cohen et al. ICS chart (2013, updated) lists every GSSP. The Anthropocene proposal (Zalasiewicz + AWG; voted down March 2024) was an attempted Holocene-Anthropocene GSSP. Without GSSPs, the geologic time scale would still be a regional patchwork.
question.explanation: GSSPs are international-vote-defined points in specific outcrops that physically embody chronostratigraphic boundaries — Cambrian-Ordovician Green Point (2000), Permian-Triassic Meishan (2001), K-Pg El Kef (1991), Holocene NorthGRIP (2009). Replace regional type localities with global reference + enable rigorous correlation worldwide. The Cohen et al. ICS chart catalogs all GSSPs.

hints: What does the bronze plaque mark?
What problem did it solve before 1976?
slides.workedSolution: GSSPs (Golden Spikes) are single stratigraphic sections + points chosen by ICS international vote + physically marked to define chronostratigraphic boundaries. Examples: PT at Meishan, K-Pg at El Kef, Cambrian-Ordovician at Green Point, Holocene in NorthGRIP ice core. They replace ambiguous regional type localities + anchor global correlation.

question.question: Building a Late Cretaceous chronology
question.prompt: You're reconstructing the Late Cretaceous (100-66 Mya) chronology of a continental section in Wyoming (Lance + Hell Creek Formations, top of the Mesozoic, ending in the K-Pg boundary). The section contains: (a) interbedded ash layers (~3 per 10 m); (b) abundant vertebrate fossils including ceratopsians + tyrannosaurs + hadrosaurs; (c) several magnetic reversals through the interval; (d) the iridium-anomaly clay marking K-Pg. Design a multi-proxy chronology. Address: (1) which dating methods you would prioritize + why (U-Pb on zircon from ash beds vs. Ar-Ar on biotite vs. biostratigraphy vs. magnetostratigraphy vs. astronomical tuning vs. chemostratigraphy); (2) the expected precision of each (U-Pb ID-TIMS can reach ±0.05% — ±35 kyr at 70 Myr); (3) how you would correlate to the **K-Pg GSSP at El Kef** + handle the iridium layer; (4) how the **Schoene 2019** dating revisions of the K-Pg interval (Chicxulub + Deccan + impact + extinction timing) should inform your interpretation; (5) what you would do if the U-Pb + Ar-Ar ages disagreed by 200 kyr; (6) how the resulting chronology would let you test hypotheses about the K-Pg extinction (dust + tsunami + Schulte 2010 review; Alvarez 1980 impact; Hildebrand 1991 Chicxulub identification).

question.question: A ¹⁴C measurement on a Late Pleistocene mammoth tusk gives ¹⁴C / ¹²C = 0.125 of modern. With $t_{1/2}$ = 5730 yr for ¹⁴C, compute the radiocarbon age to the nearest 100 years.
question.hint: $t = (t_{1/2} / \ln 2) \ln(1/0.125) = (5730 / 0.6931) \times \ln 8 = 8267 \times 2.0794 \approx 17190$ yr. (Note: Libby radiocarbon ages are calibrated to calendar years via IntCal — ~17 ka would be in the Last Glacial Maximum interval, consistent with mammoth dates in central North America.)

question.prompt: In ≤140 words, explain the geologic time scale's architecture (eons → eras → periods → epochs) + the three orthogonal methods (radiometric + bio- + magnetostratigraphy) that calibrate it, + the role of GSSPs.
question.rubric: Mentions: GTS hierarchy: Eons (Hadean → Archean → Proterozoic → Phanerozoic) → Eras (Paleozoic + Mesozoic + Cenozoic within Phanerozoic) → Periods → Epochs. Anthropocene proposal (Zalasiewicz + AWG; voted down March 2024). Calibration uses three orthogonal methods: (1) **Radiometric dating** — U-Pb on zircon (Patterson 1956 dated Earth at 4.55 Gyr), Ar-Ar, ¹⁴C (Libby Nobel 1960), cosmogenic, U-series; gives absolute ages. (2) **Biostratigraphy** — index fossils (Smith 1815 faunal succession) — trilobites, conodonts, ammonites, foraminifera. (3) **Magnetostratigraphy** — GPTS calibrated by Cande + Kent. Walther's Law + sequence stratigraphy interpret facies. Every boundary is anchored by a **GSSP Golden Spike** — single physical point voted by ICS — examples Meishan PT, El Kef K-Pg, NorthGRIP Holocene. Cohen et al. ICS chart is the global standard. Concludes: when all methods converge, the GTS provides the most reliable chronological framework in any science.
